scope: Research-only original-source critical review of 2026 selection-free whole-genome transplant into genomically inactivated but metabolically functioning bacterial chassis versus abiotic construction; no experiments

source.citation: Seidel ZP et al. Selection-free whole genome transplantation revives dead microbes. bioRxiv version 1, 14 March 2026.
source.evidence_grade: E2-depth indexed original main Results/selected Methods/figure legends/Discussion, caveated: direct full-text open 403 or browser challenge; complete contiguous final main text, supplements, raw figure observations and E3 replication not inspected
source.institutional_metadata_discrepancy: NIST catalog cites Nature; as of this review verified original with DOI 10.64898/2026.03.13.711674 is a bioRxiv version 1 preprint. Do not infer peer-reviewed Nature article without original journal DOI.
source.rights: bioRxiv source version reports CC BY 4.0, original critical paraphrase only; figures/raw files and supplementary archives not reused
source.program: JCVI and NIST; overlaps older JCVI Gibson 2010 transplantation research program
source.founding_chassis: M. capricolum recipient with native genome replication inactivated by DNA crosslinking but preassembled functional transcription/translation and membranes retained; restriction system engineered for donor compatibility
source.donor_genome: Prepared M. mycoides complete genome from living bacterial/yeast intermediates
positive_outcomes: Donor-genome genotype bacterial colonies emerged after recipient native genomic DNA disabling
Growth on plates without antibiotic marker selection plus blue/white genotype and PCR controls
Transplantation persisted under conditions where replicating plasmid transformation was undetected
Two different genome DNA crosslinking routes supported some transplantation: MMC and psoralen photoactivation
negative_outcomes: Conventional WGT was confounded by homologous recombination of resistance markers in previous non-Mycoides/intraspecies attempts, misleadingly scoring partial donor DNA transfer as whole-genome replacement
Original recipient survival after genome-inactivating treatment not completely zero: approximately 7200 viable out of initially ~10 billion
Total transplant colonies decreased rather than increased after damage: 68 plus/minus 59 to 25 plus/minus 19 in reported comparison
No transplants in strongest MMC treatment regime in tested series
Psoralen had narrow successful condition range, increased photoactivation lowered WGT yield
Whole-genome transplantation across distant bacterial taxa or into nonliving assembled cytoplasm not demonstrated

quantitative_original_results.transplant_number_drop: ~10-fold in treatment-series comparison; separate from N=7 vs N=6 comparison

selected_bacterial_vs_yeast_genome_prepa.negative: much lower yeast-sourced yields, sometimes only one donor colony in treated arm

control_evidence: Conventional replicative plasmid transformation suppressed even as WGT survived under matched genomic-inactivation exposure
Blue donor and white residual recipient genotype exemplars validated with multiplex PCR and differentiated antibiotic growth
Untreated recipient lawn on antibiotic-free plates masked donor transplants
Alternative crosslinker supports a plausible genomic lesion mechanism but did not independently recreate a new cell origin
alternative_explanations: Rare remaining viable recipients enriched for WGT competence may contribute some colonies; no complete single-cell ancestry inventory
Different genome versus plasmid transformation properties may complicate exact inference about per-cell nonviability
Already active old transcription/translation/membrane apparatus, deliberately retained, supplies the bootstrap; genuinely abiotic materials not tested
Highly non-general Mycoides-clade compatibility and engineered recipient restriction-system change

context_only.role: Previously E2 main primary in Pass45: genome transplantation into living native cytoplasm; overlapping JCVI team, not independent 2026 replication

Already reviewed Gaut et al 2026 E2-partial preprint in Pass40: mechanically cycled liposomes five times and separate engineered cell division; preassembled PURE replenished and no spontaneous adaptive mutation observed
Existing Pass40 E1 context only: Restrepo Sierra et al 2026 integrated six protein program and phospholipid synthesis; not upgraded here or counted as independent genome rescue replication

independence_conclusion: 2026 Seidel is one JCVI/NIST program with ancestry overlap to 2010 Gibson, not E3; Gaut and Restrepo Sierra investigate different endpoints; no pooled evidence of fully autonomous abiotic reproductive founding

semantic_boundaries.genomic_death: Loss of recipient cell's ability to form colonies with inactivated own genomic replication
semantic_boundaries.residual_activity: Intact active resident transcription and translation, metabolism, and membranes are intentionally preserved
semantic_boundaries.selection_free: Free from ANTIBIOTIC resistance selection in plating, not unassisted founding or absence of differential survival
semantic_boundaries.efficiency_denominator: Treated viable-recipient counts in denominator dramatically decline; absolute number of successful transplant colonies decreases
semantic_boundaries.derived_reproduction: Cell division following reprogramming is genuine but not proof of initial constructor from nonliving ingredients

next_primary_question: Find independent founder-resolved original experiments ruling out residual viable recipients or measuring chromosomal and machinery provenance outside a single JCVI chassis; absent adequate primary evidence, record source gap rather than counterfeit replication
publication_gate: Successful CI on exact reviewed PR head, no main or head drift before expected-head merge, independently verified successful resulting main push run
